description: No Renovate age gate here: Renovate can't date a lock file refresh, so a gate would hold it forever. npm enforces the cooldown instead, through min-release-age in .npmrc, and it is the only side that sees the transitive versions a refresh picks.

A refresh is only true of the tree it resolved against, so every merge to main leaves this branch describing a package.json that has moved. Rebasing on the base branch regenerates it, which keeps its green check a statement about the merge someone is actually about to make.

packageRules.description: A major needs a proper read of its changelog, which rarely happens the week it lands. Park it on the dashboard so it stops holding a concurrency slot, and tick it there when someone is ready to do that work.
A lock file refresh carries no update anyone is waiting on, so it is created last and takes one of the concurrency slots above only when a real update does not need it.
Manage GitHub Actions SHA pins by hand. A digest-bump PR is a branch in this repo, so CI, E2E with TENKI_API_KEY included, would run the new action code before anyone reviews it.
.nvmrc sets Node 24 for development, Renovate and CI, so its types stay on 24; move this with it.
Batch non-major devDependency updates into one PR.
vite and its plugins move together; @vitejs/plugin-react 6 requires vite ^8.
eslint and @eslint/* release in lockstep, and typescript-eslint has to support the eslint it runs under.
convex-test declares convex as a peer, so the two move together.
@convex-dev/auth declares @auth/core as a peer, and on 0.x any release can break, so the two move together and outside the batch.
Each Tenki SDK release gets its own PR; the e2e suite runs against it and a human merges it.
